transplant_window.citation: Punjab 2026 paddy schedule (Zone 3, incl. Fazilka and Sri Muktsar Sahib, from June 5), reported by Babushahi, 29 Apr 2026; PAU Package of Practices Kharif 2026 (transplant 20 Jun-10 Jul; PR 126 by 15 Jul)
transplant_window.note: Start = government zone-3 opening date; end = PAU's latest date for PR 126 (https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf).

awd_window_days_after_transplant.citation: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank, AWD; PAU Package of Practices Kharif 2026
awd_window_days_after_transplant.note: Start 14: IRRI starts AWD 1-2 weeks after transplanting; PAU keeps water standing for 2 weeks. End 85: PAU stops irrigating about 2 weeks before maturity; PR 126 matures ~93 days after transplanting (79) and PR 130-133 at 105-111 days (91-97). 85 sits inside 79-97.

cycle_days.citation: Shah et al., Machine Learning for Sustainable Rice Production, AAAI 2026
cycle_days.note: Punjab AWD fields are irrigated 'typically every 4-10 days'.

drained_fraction_of_cycle.citation: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank, AWD fact sheet; ARCC Agricultural Reviews R-2043 (AWD review)
drained_fraction_of_cycle.note: No source states the fraction directly. IRRI: non-flooded days per AWD cycle range from 1 to more than 10; a review reports the best schedule as about 3 days of drainage after ponded water disappears (https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-reviews/R-2043). With cycle_days 4-10, about 2-3 dry days gives 0.3-0.5 (capped at 0.5, since PAU keeps fields ponded more often than dry). Reviewed by Ishaan (SPEC A4).

cf_single_drain_prob.citation: India Third Biennial Update Report (MoEFCC 2021), via CEEW 'What reduces emissions in sustainable rice cultivation', Table 1
cf_single_drain_prob.note: Single aeration 16.44% vs continuous flooding 15.89% of India's rice area: 16.44 / (16.44 + 15.89) = 0.51 of non-AWD irrigated fields drain once. National figure, not Punjab.

per_pass_accuracy.citation: Islam, Oyoshi and Takeuchi, Remote Sensing 18(8):1183, 2026
per_pass_accuracy.note: ALOS-2 L-band full-pol + Freeman-Durden, 704 fields in Naogaon, Bangladesh: 94% early, 80% under dense canopy. Not NISAR and not Punjab; dual-pol is expected to do worse (Jin et al. 2026, https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18132136).

cf_false_flag_max.note: A continuously flooded field may be flagged as AWD at most 10% of the time.

awd_miss_max.note: Call a field not consistent with AWD only if an AWD field would have shown a drained look at least 90% of the time.

dsr_min_early_looks.note: At least two clear looks before Jul 15 before giving any DSR signal.

sentence: With 10 passes, a field practicing AWD is caught drained at least 3 times 37% of the time; a continuously flooded field shows that 5% of the time.
